is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus sensu stricto (An. funestus) collected in northern Nigeria (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper genotypes GSTe2 L119F (Page 5, Section 2.8), Vgsc L1014F/S (Page 6, Section 2.10), Ace-1 G119S (Page 6, Section 2.9), and Ace-1 N485I (Page 6, Section 2.9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts are provided for GSTe2 L119F in F0 females (Page 8, Section 3.7: 13 RS, 14 RR, 7 SS) and for F1 survivors/dead (Page 9, Section 3.7). Absence of Vgsc 1014F/S (0/30, Page 10), Ace-1 G119S (0/24, Page 9), and Ace-1 N485I (0/24, Page 10) is also reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Gajerar Giwa, Katsina State, Nigeria (Page 2, Section 2.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original collection and genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to Gajerar Giwa (13°11'57.1" N 7°45'53.5" E), Katsina State, Nigeria (Page 2, Section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected between 17–20 November 2018 (Page 2, Section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper describes the study as primary data and notes that An. funestus in this region has been neglected for decades (Page 2).

supplement.evidence: While supplementary files (S1, Table S1-S3) are mentioned, the critical genotype counts and site information are provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: The study investigates insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus from the Sahel region of northern Nigeria (Katsina State). It reports high resistance to pyrethroids, DDT, and bendiocarb. Molecular analysis identified a high frequency of the GSTe2 L119F mutation (allele frequency ~0.84), while Vgsc L1014F/S, Ace-1 G119S, and Ace-1 N485I mutations were absent in the tested population.
